data.name: Urlaubsflug Simulator – Holiday Flight Simulator
data.detailed_description:
Without doubt flying virtual aircraft from your PC is one of the most interesting simulations – at the same time, it is one with a very steep learning curve. Holiday Flight Simulator, though, makes it especially easy to relive the last holiday trip from the cockpit’s view, even for less experienced PC pilots. Unlike more complex flight simulations, Holiday Flight Simulator was designed from the ground up to enable beginners to successfully complete a flight with less effort and learning. Advanced flight simulation enthusiasts in turn have a straightforward all-in-one solution at hand, including lots of airports right from the start.

The player can take place behind the control stick of one of the most well known airliners: the Airbus A320. Its cockpit places all the important functions and systems at the player’s disposal – voice recordings from real air traffic help create the appropriate atmosphere. Additionally, the simulation includes a Beechcraft Baron for short range and training flights.

Holiday Flight Simulator comes with 9 travel destinations out of the box, including the airports of Düsseldorf, Palma de Mallorca, London Heathrow, and Nice. Their 3D models are of high quality and rich in details. They also feature movable objects – luggage carts, busses, pushback trucks, jetways, etc. create lively apron scenery. A day and night cycle makes these sceneries appear in the right mood.

In the beginning, players can choose whether they want to fly freely between two airports or experience long-term thrill in the career mode.



Aircraft:

  • Airbus A 320
  • Beechcraft Baron

Flight area:

  • Europe

Airports:

  • Hamburg
  • Düsseldorf
  • Zürich
  • Paris Orly
  • London Heathrow
  • Nizza
  • Palma
  • Kos
  • Antalya

Game modes:

  • Tutorial
  • Random flight
  • Route selection
  • Career

Other:

  • Beginner friendly
  • Achievements
  • Day and night modes
  • Animated pilot models in the cockpit
  • Three camera views
  • Original voice recordings with real pilots
    [*Liveries of various European airlines[/list]

    „Holiday Flight Simulator“ and „Ready for Take Off“ are identical products.

reviews.review:
Urlaubsflug Simulator – Holiday Flight Simulator takes a lighter and more approachable route to civilian aviation, focusing on the fantasy of piloting passenger aircraft between popular European vacation destinations. Developed by Caipirinha Games and published by SimWare Simulations, it is clearly designed for players who like the idea of flight simulation but may not want to deal with the enormous learning curve associated with more technically demanding simulators. Its smaller scope works in its favor for beginners, although experienced virtual pilots will likely notice its limitations fairly quickly.

The Airbus A320 is the centerpiece of the experience and provides the game with its commercial aviation identity. Instead of recreating every system with study-level complexity, the aircraft is presented in a way that makes basic operation easier to understand. This means newcomers can concentrate more on the experience of taking off, navigating a route, approaching an airport, and landing rather than spending hours learning individual cockpit systems. A Beechcraft Baron is also available, offering a smaller aircraft that provides a welcome alternative to flying the much larger passenger jet.

The destination selection is built around European holiday travel. Players can visit airports associated with Hamburg, Düsseldorf, Zürich, Paris Orly, London Heathrow, Nice, Palma, Kos, and Antalya. It is not an enormous world to explore, but the selection gives the game a focused identity. Ground activity such as buses, luggage vehicles, pushback trucks, and jetways helps airports feel less static, while the day and night cycle adds atmospheric variation. Landing at an illuminated airport after dark can feel noticeably different from completing the same journey during daylight.

There are several ways to approach the flying itself. The tutorial is particularly valuable because the game is intended to be more accessible than hardcore aviation simulations. Players can select routes, participate in randomly generated flights, progress through a career, or simply enjoy the sightseeing aspect of flying. Profiles keep track of statistics such as flying time and career progress, while achievements provide additional objectives. These elements give players reasons to continue flying after becoming familiar with the basic controls, though the relatively small selection of aircraft and airports eventually creates repetition.

Atmosphere is one of the more appealing parts of the package. Animated pilots, multiple camera perspectives, airline liveries, active ground equipment, and recorded voices from actual pilots all contribute to the sensation of operating within a functioning aviation environment. The presentation is understandably dated compared with modern flight simulators, however. Scenery, lighting, environmental detail, and aircraft visuals cannot compete with newer simulation technology, so anyone expecting photorealistic landscapes or a huge recreation of the world will need to adjust their expectations.

The simplified simulation model creates an interesting balance. Players unfamiliar with aviation can learn the essentials without being overwhelmed by procedures, but serious simulation enthusiasts may find the aircraft systems too shallow. The experience works better as an introduction to virtual passenger aviation than as a highly technical recreation of real-world Airbus operations. This accessibility makes short sessions enjoyable because there is less preparation required before getting into the air.

Content variety is the more significant weakness. Two aircraft and a modest collection of destinations can only provide so much long-term diversity. Career progression and random flights help extend the experience, but they cannot entirely disguise the limited geographical and aircraft selection. The simulation is therefore best enjoyed as a focused aviation title rather than a platform intended to provide hundreds or thousands of hours of continually changing flight experiences.

Steam Deck compatibility is officially listed as Unknown or Unverified rather than Verified or Playable. The game was designed primarily for Windows PCs, and its cockpit-oriented controls make a conventional keyboard, mouse, controller, or dedicated flight setup a more natural choice. It may be possible to experiment with Steam Deck control configurations or compatibility layers, but players should not assume that the complete experience will function smoothly on Valve's handheld without adjustments.

Overall, Urlaubsflug Simulator – Holiday Flight Simulator has an appealing concept that works particularly well for newcomers interested in commercial aviation. Its A320 focus, European vacation routes, accessible controls, tutorial, career progression, active airports, authentic pilot recordings, and alternative flight modes provide a pleasant introduction to the genre. Aging visuals, simplified aircraft systems, a restricted selection of destinations, and limited aircraft variety keep it from competing with deeper flight simulators, but that was never really its purpose. For players seeking an uncomplicated taste of European passenger flying without the enormous technical commitment of a hardcore simulator, it remains an interesting if noticeably dated experience.

Rating: 6/10
